findings.title: Possible hard-coded credential

findings.title: Network retrieval combined with code execution
findings.description: The same file contains both a network retrieval pattern and a dynamic execution pattern. This combination merits review and is not by itself proof of malicious intent.

evidence.snippet: Write-VerboseLog -Fore White -Back Blue "`$webResponse = Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri $UriText -Body $BodyText -ContentType $ContentTypeText -Headers `$Headers -Method $MethodText -Proxy ""$script:proxy"" -UseDefaultCredentials:$UseDefaultCredentials"  …  if ($Start) { Start-Process -FilePath $url }

findings.title: Plain text password parameter is declared
findings.description: Parameter '$Password' should not use String type but either SecureString or PSCredential, otherwise it increases the chance to expose this sensitive information.

findings.title: Separate username and password parameters are declared
findings.description: Function 'Set-Headers' has both Username and Password parameters. Either set the type of the Password parameter to SecureString or replace the Username and Password parameters with a Credential parameter of type PSCredential. If using a Credential parameter in PowerShell 4.0 or earlier, please define a credential transformation attribute after the PSCredential type attribute.
